title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention (timeouts)
author: Aisha Raman
description: Background: production traffic analysis showed intermittent starvation of low-latency, small-request workloads when the continuous batcher became filled with long-running high-token requests. The previous FIFO-style admission and a single global timeout resulted in long tail latencies for priority-sensitive routes. Motivation: reduce p95/p99 tail without regressing aggregate throughput for large-batch customers and keep behavior predictable across Dedicated/Hosted modes. Core changes: 1) Scheduler refactor to use a lightweight weighted queueing approach (per-priority buckets) and an aging promotion mechanism that increases effective weight as requests wait; 2) Introduced configurable timeouts and per-priority max_pending caps (config keys: fairness_window_ms, starvation_threshold_ms, max_pending_per_priority, preemption_budget, global_request_timeout_ms); 3) Implemented a starvation detector that preempts a small amount of in-flight batch capacity to accept promoted/aged requests when thresholds are crossed; 4) Dynamic timeout heuristics: timeouts are adjusted using short-term seq_len percentiles (p50/p90) so short sequences avoid being held by large sequences; 5) Added extensive unit/integration tests and a benchmark harness to validate tail reduction and throughput; 6) Updated docs and runtime config examples. Implementation notes: scheduler logic moved from runtime/continuous_batcher/scheduler.rs to runtime/continuous_batcher/scheduler_v2.rs with a small public API shim to ease rollout. Key algorithm sketch: - maintain per-priority ring queues; - when dequeuing, compute effective_weight = base_weight + age_factor (age_factor grows linearly after starvation_threshold_ms); - if effective_weight of waiting requests exceeds a configurable preemption_budget, attempt to slice one in-flight batch (respecting min_batch_size) and insert promoted requests; - enforce per-priority max_pending caps to protect control-plane/backpressure-sensitive routes. Default conservative values chosen to avoid oscillation; flags available for aggressive tuning in Dedicated. Benchmarks: on internal perf lab (A100 cluster, mixed short/long workload) we see median unchanged, p95 reduced by ~10-15% and p99 reduced by ~12-18% for latency-sensitive routes while throughput impact <2% in steady-state. Testing: new unit tests for aging/promotion, integration tests that simulate mixed traffic and assert no starvation, and end-to-end benchmark harness added under benchmarks/continuous_batcher. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag continuous_batcher.fairness_v2 and enabled via config for canary hosts; watch metrics added to console (queue_age_seconds, promoted_requests_count, preempt_events). Risk and mitigation: preemption could reduce throughput for large-batch workloads; mitigated by preemption_budget and min_batch_size. CI: initial run failed a flaky scheduling unit test (test_scheduler_timeout) - root cause was a race in the fake clock test harness; fixed and re-ran. Changelog and docs: docs/continuous-batcher.md updated with example configs and migration notes. Request: merge to main with squash; backport candidate for the next 2.1.x runtime patch.

release_notes: Improves continuous batcher scheduler fairness and prevents starvation for latency-sensitive routes; introduces stability flags: fairness_v2, config knobs for timeouts and preemption; default behavior is conservative to avoid throughput regressions.
notes_for_backport: Backport candidate: include scheduler_v2 logic and conservative defaults; skip benchmark harness and docs in patch backport.
